primary.title: Tata Sons may shift listing onus to board, chair
primary.description: Mumbai: Tata Sons is understood to be preparing for a board meeting on November 26, armed with a detailed statement on its listing plans vetted by senior advocate Harish Salve that puts the onus on the board and chairman to comply with the Reserve Bank of India's instruction. The meeting is expected to bring into sharper focus the differences between Tata Sons and its principal shareholder, Tata Trusts, over whether the group holding company should remain privately held or comply with RBI's regulatory requirement to list it.The central bank sent a letter to Tata Sons on November 16 that it must comply with all applicable regulations governing upper layer non-banking financial companies, "including the requirement of listing by your company." This was in response to Tata Sons' October 6 communication seeking RBI's guidance on compliance with the regulations.Also Read: Tata Sons board to review Air India turnaround progressMonetisation of SP Group StakeTata group's holding company is likely to detail the listing strategy and how it proposes to take this forward at the November 26 meeting, said executives aware of the matter.135970562Tata Sons may also turn down an alternative restructuring proposal backed by Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata, arguing that RBI's rejection of the application to surrender its registration as a core investment company has left it with little scope to avoid a stock market listing. The legal presentation is expected to emphasise that the board and its chairman have a responsibility to initiate the compliance process, rather than pursue alternatives that could delay it, people familiar with the developments said.Also Read: Darius Khambata hits back at Venu Srinivasan, Vijay SinghTata Sons did not comment.Chairman N Chandrasekaran is likely to hold a private meeting with Shapoor Mistry ahead of the board meeting, to directly discuss the monetisation of Shapoorji Pallonji Group's 18.4% stake in Tata Sons and the group's funding requirements.Tata Sons' position is that monetisation of the Mistry-led SP Group's stake is not a matter for Noel Tata to address in his capacity as Tata Trusts chairman, according to people familiar with the company's thinking.SP Group, which is urgently seeking funds to repay borrowings, wants Tata Sons to buy back about ₹25,000 crore worth of its shares over the next 24 months. Noel Tata tabled this request from SP Group to the Tata Sons board at the last meeting on September 17."There cannot be any delay in the matter of listing. It is now a regulatory matter and the directive from RBI is clear. The restructuring proposal will be disposed of by Tata Sons. Tata Trusts had sent the restructuring proposal directly to RBI in September and Tata Sons will not consider the matter at all," said an executive.The holding company may also seek to finalise a date for its much-delayed AGM.Tata Trusts, which owns about 66% of Tata Sons, has been pushing for an alternative restructuring plan that could help the holding company avoid a listing. Noel Tata is expected to argue that the board should challenge RBI's September decision and reconsider the proposal submitted to the central bank.The proposal envisages merging Tata Electronics Systems Solutions and Tata Consulting Engineers with Tata Sons, giving the holding company an operating income stream and potentially changing its regulatory profile. The restructuring requires corporate, shareholder and regulatory approvals.Tata Sons has been classified as an upper-layer NBFC due to its large asset size and status as a core investment company. Under RBI's scale-based regulatory framework, upper-layer NBFCs are required to list their equity shares on a recognised stock exchange within three years of being identified in that category.Ashish K Singh, managing partner at Capstone Legal, said Tata Sons' only option to challenge RBI's order was to file a writ petition before the Bombay High Court, with the company itself being the appropriate party to initiate proceedings as the entity directly affected by the directive. "The decision, however, would have to be taken by the Tata Sons board collectively, and no such decision has been taken so far," Singh said. "The absence of a quorum at Tata Trusts was also an additional factor, limiting its influence over decision-making at Tata Sons," he said.Tata Trusts has a meeting scheduled for November 20 to revisit its opposition to the listing and discuss restructuring alternative. Neville Tata and Bhaskar Bhat are expected to support Noel Tata's position against listing and favour exploring the restructuring route, the people cited earlier said.
